author: vivekananda
period: Published in 1896, based on classes given in New York in 1895–1896
summary: Vivekananda's influential presentation of Patanjali's yoga, with lectures on practice and his own rendering and commentary on the Yoga Sutras.
whyRead: It was one of the books that introduced yoga to the West, and it shaped how meditation and yoga were understood for decades. Read it as a modern interpretation of the Yoga Sutras, with its own emphases on psychology and science.
questions: Can meditation be studied like a science?
What is the relation between breath and mind?

keyTeachings.title: Yoga as a science of mind
keyTeachings.text: Vivekananda presents raja yoga as an experimental method: its claims are to be tested by practice rather than accepted on faith.

keyTeachings.title: The eight limbs
keyTeachings.text: He explains Patanjali's eight limbs, from ethics and posture to concentration, meditation and samadhi.

keyTeachings.title: Prana and the subtle body
keyTeachings.text: He discusses prana and the subtle channels, blending Patanjali with hatha and tantric ideas, a blend characteristic of his interpretation.

relatedTexts.note: Source of some of the subtle-body ideas it draws on
